title: Portable native elliptic L-function boundary
objective: Expose eclib root numbers and implement a host-independent batched FLINT/Arb central-derivative accelerator with Node adapter and native tests

exceptions: Arb foreign-library adapter and compact batched numerical primitive; the readable mathematics and dynamic fallback live in ordinary Python

handoff.summary: Commit 5a43cbff exposes eclib global root numbers and a portable C/FLINT-Arb completed central-Lambda derivative jet through ecRootNumber and ecCompletedCentralDerivatives. The jet returns consecutive actual derivatives with exact functional-equation parity, decimal arithmetic-ball diagnostics, a separate coefficient-tail bound, and explicit coefficient/resource status. Focused native tests cover canonical normalization, ranks 0/1/2, rational Q-isomorphic models, insufficient coefficients, and oversized conductors; the complete packages/flint test suite passes on Linux x64.
risks: The Arb balls enclose arithmetic rounding only. The coefficient tail is reported separately, and the unproved trapezoid/grid discretization error means rigorous is deliberately false; the Python layer must use precision/grid stability checks and must sum independent error contributions.

Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64 runtime receipts remain pending. The implementation uses the existing C17/Node-API/FLINT build path and avoids POSIX-only APIs; the integration lane will validate Windows once the shared checkout is free.

pnpm test:portable fails only because architecture/native-code inventory metrics for packages/flint/src/addon.c are stale after this lane's export additions. This lane was explicitly told not to edit architecture inventories.
The simple all-coefficients-at-every-grid-node implementation is O(KL). A future measured optimization may use node-dependent cutoffs if their omitted tails are included explicitly.
next_steps: Integration lane: classify the new native ABI/kernel and refresh architecture inventory metrics, then rerun pnpm test:portable and pnpm architecture:check.
Integration lane: run the focused native test and build on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64 and record receipts.
Math lane: combine arithmetic radius and coefficient-tail bounds additively, retain the non-rigorous status, and perform completed-to-raw gamma convolution in ordinary Python.
After integration, run the full pnpm test:native and pnpm test:sea suites; this lane's cold dependency rebuilds were interrupted to avoid delaying the committed handoff.
